title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Problem II (previous page) converts an alternating power series s = x/α − x²/β + x³/γ − … into a continued fraction. It uses the tails t, u, … and the relation s = x/α − xt, which gives x/s = α + α²x/(β − αx + β²x/(γ − βx + …)).

§33: Euler replaces x by x/y, so the series becomes s = x/(αy) − x²/(βy²) + … . This gives x/(sy) = α + α²(x/y)/(β − αx/y + β²(x/y)/(γ − βx/y + …)). He then clears the partial fractions. Multiply the numerator and denominator of the first partial quotient by y, and do the same at every deeper level. Each later numerator then becomes β²xy, γ²xy, …, while the first stays α²x.

§34 (Theorem IV): multiplying through by y gives the homogeneous form
x/s = αy + α²xy/(βy − αx + β²xy/(γy − βx + γ²xy/(δy − γx + δ²xy/(εy − δx + …)))).
In modern terms this is Euler's 1748 continued-fraction formula for an alternating series, applied to a power series with coefficients 1/α_k, written homogeneously in (x, y).

§35: With α_k = k, the log series ln(1 + x/y) gives
x/ln(1 + x/y) = y + 1xy/(2y − x + 4xy/(3y − 2x + 9xy/(4y − 3x + …))).

§36: Start from t·arctan t = t² − t⁴/3 + t⁶/5 − …. Put t² = x/y, so the coefficients are α_k = 2k − 1. This gives
√(xy)/arctan√(x/y) = y + xy/(3y − x + 9xy/(5y − 3x + 25xy/(7y − 5x + …))).
The example x = 1, y = 3 uses arctan(1/√3) = π/6. It leads, on the next page, to 6√3/π = 3 + 1·3/(8 + 3·9/(12 + 3·25/(16 + …))).

The page serves the paper's programme of turning series for logarithms and arctangents into continued fractions that yield expansions of π and ln 2.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. I verified the clearing of the partial fractions, Theorem IV, the log continued fraction and the arctan continued fraction. Numerically, 3 + 3/(8 + 27/(12 + 75/(16 + 147/20))) ≈ 3.3069, against 6√3/π ≈ 3.3080, so the example is consistent.

ideas.what: Conversion of an alternating power series with coefficients 1/α_k into a continued fraction via the tail recursion, written homogeneously in x and y (Theorem IV).
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (equivalence of series and continued fractions)
ideas.where_published: Introductio I ch. 18; E593 itself (Opera Omnia I.16)

ideas.modern_name: Euler-type continued fraction for the logarithm

ideas.what: Continued fraction for √(xy)/arctan√(x/y), with the special case 6√3/π.
ideas.modern_name: Euler continued fraction for arctan (Brouncker/Euler type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (building on Brouncker and Wallis for 4/π)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine homogenization of Euler's well-known 1748 series-to-continued-fraction transformation, with standard log and arctan examples. All of it is published and recognized in E593 and the Introductio.
transcription_corrections: Next page, first formula: the left side should read 6√3/π (continuing 'habebitur ista fractio continua: 6√3/π = …'), not 4√2/π. The numerators 1·3, 3·9, 3·25 are correct (xy·k² with xy = 3).
